title: Price It Before You Leave
premise: Ray, a skilled solo handyman, keeps losing jobs and money because he prices from his gut and promises to 'text a number later'. One afternoon in a homeowner's bathroom he prices a tile repair on the spot with the Estimator app, turns his phone around, and closes the job before he leaves the house.
logline: A gut-feel handyman who always underquotes must give a nervous homeowner a real price on the spot, before a bigger contractor's polished quote wins the job.

timeline: Ray Delgado works construction crews for 15 years, then goes solo 3 years ago.
He wins work on referrals but loses about one in three jobs while he 'figures out a number'.
Last month he underquoted a deck repair and worked two days for free.
Today: Linda Park's cracked bathroom tile, with a contractor's quote due tomorrow.
era_rules: Present day, United States, prices in US dollars.
Everyone has a smartphone; the Estimator app works offline in a basement with no signal.
Homeowners compare quotes online and expect a number the same day.

factions.name: Independent handymen
factions.goal: fair pay for skilled work and a full calendar
factions.power_over: availability and craft: they can start this week, big contractors can't

factions.name: Homeowners
factions.goal: a fair price they can trust, fast
factions.power_over: they pick who gets the job and they talk to their neighbors

factions.name: Big contractors
factions.goal: win every mid-size job in the neighborhood
factions.power_over: polished PDF quotes and brand trust that make solo trades look improvised

world_rules: Every price on screen comes from the real Estimator calculation for the sample tile job: materials $331.00, standard price $1,360.87, budget $1,156.74, premium $1,633.04.
No stopwatches or claims of a specific number of seconds - the film shows speed, it never states it.
The phone screen always shows the real Estimator UI, composited in post from motion-studio renders.
Ray never badmouths competitors; he wins by being clear.

characters.name: Ray Delgado
characters.flaw: Hates paperwork, so he quotes from his gut and underprices his own time.
characters.want: To close jobs on the spot at a price that actually pays him.
characters.vocal_cadence: Low, unhurried, short sentences; says numbers plainly; never fills silence.
behavioral_ticks: runs a thumb along tile grout when thinking
taps the phone twice before turning it around
nods once when a deal is done

characters.name: Linda Park
characters.flaw: Assumes anyone without a printed quote is guessing.
characters.want: A fair price she understands, today, so she can stop worrying about it.
characters.vocal_cadence: Polite, quick, slightly anxious; asks questions that end in a small laugh.
behavioral_ticks: holds her mug with both hands
relaxes her shoulders when she trusts someone
